scholarships.title: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
scholarships.official_source: Gates Cambridge Trust, with the University of Cambridge

existing.description: A fully funded graduate education for future leaders committed to improving the lives of others.
eligibility: Citizen of any country outside the United Kingdom
Applying for a PhD at Cambridge (full-time or part-time; a part-time PhD funding pilot continues)
Applying for a full-time one-year postgraduate course, with some exceptions
Current Cambridge students may apply for a new postgraduate course, for example an MPhil student applying for a PhD
Current Gates Cambridge Scholars may apply for a second scholarship for a new degree
Not eligible: any undergraduate degree such as BA or BA affiliated
Not eligible: part-time degrees other than the PhD

Not eligible: professional development and non-standard degrees including MBA, EMBA and Global EMBA, MFin, Executive Master of Accounting, Business Doctorate (BusD), PGCE, MBBChir Clinical Studies, the six-year part-time MD, Graduate Course in Medicine (A101), and Master of Conservation of Easel Painting
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to citizens of any country outside the United Kingdom applying for a full-time or part-time PhD, a full-time MLitt, or a full-time one-year postgraduate course at the University of Cambridge. Undergraduate degrees, MASt courses, part-time degrees other than the PhD, and a list of professional and non-standard degrees are excluded.
benefits: Maintenance allowance of Â£23,152 for 12 months at the 2026-27 rate, up to 4 years for PhD scholars
Inbound visa costs and Immigration Health Surcharge
Discretionary academic development, dependent children, fieldwork, maternity/paternity and hardship funding
Membership of a scholar community of about 250 current Scholars and more than 1,700 alumni from 116 countries
coverage: The University Composition Fee at the appropriate rate
A maintenance allowance for a single student of Â£23,152 for 12 months at the 2026-27 rate, pro rata for shorter courses, for up to 4 years for PhD scholars
One economy single airfare at both the beginning and the end of the course
Inbound visa costs and the Immigration Health Surcharge
Discretionary academic development funding from up to Â£750 to up to Â£4,000 depending on course length, for conferences and courses
Discretionary Dependent Children Allowance of up to Â£12,793 per annum for one child and up to Â£18,244 per annum for two or more children, with no funding for a partner
Discretionary funding to keep the normal maintenance allowance during fieldwork on a PhD
Discretionary maternity and paternity funding allowing study to be intermitted for up to 6 months while the maintenance allowance continues
Discretionary hardship funding for unforeseen difficulties
requirements: Submit one combined admission and funding application through the University of Cambridge Graduate Application Portal
Complete the admission to a course and College place sections and the Gates Cambridge funding section
Meet the 11:59pm UK time deadline for the round that applies to you
Have all references submitted by the deadline, including for the US round
Disclose any employer salary or substantial other scholarship to the Trust
Accept a scholarship offer within 72 hours
documents: Combined admission and funding application via the University of Cambridge Graduate Application Portal
Completed admission to a course and College place sections of the application
Completed Gates Cambridge section of the funding part of the application
All references submitted by the application deadline
application_method: University of Cambridge Graduate Application Portal (single combined admission and funding form)
existing.selection_notes: The four published selection criteria are outstanding intellectual ability, reasons for choice of course, a commitment to improving the lives of others, and leadership potential. Academic departments at Cambridge nominate only the most academically outstanding applicants. Around 70 full-cost scholarships are awarded each year, approximately two-thirds to PhD students, with approximately a third of awards available in the US round and the rest in the International round.
existing.best_fit: Academically outstanding citizens of countries outside the UK seeking full funding for a Cambridge PhD, MLitt or one-year postgraduate degree, with a clear commitment to improving the lives of others.
existing.notes: The Â£23,152 figure is the published maintenance allowance for a single student for 12 months at the 2026-27 rate and sits on top of the separately assessed University Composition Fee, so it is not the total value of the award. Around 70 awards are made per year. Bench fees and the cost of scientific equipment or similar academic resources are not covered by the Trust and are expected to be met by the Cambridge academic department.
existing.duration: Up to four years for PhD scholars; the maintenance allowance is paid for 12 months and pro rata for shorter courses
existing.application_period: 2027/8 entry. Applications opened 11 September 2026. US round closes 14 October 2026 with outcomes by 14 December 2026 and scholarships offered by early February 2027. International round closes either 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 depending on the course, with outcomes by 8 March 2027 and scholarships offered by early April 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Two selection rounds. US citizens resident in the USA: applications opened 11 September 2026 and the deadline is Wednesday 14 October 2026, with the full application submitted by 11:59pm UK time. All other eligible applicants: apply by the Course Funding Deadline in the University Course Directory, which is either Tuesday 8 December 2026 or Wednesday 6 January 2027 depending on the course.
existing.program_type: Full-cost postgraduate scholarship at the University of Cambridge

existing.description: The scholarship applies to both full- and part-time study.
eligibility: Be making a new PhD application; current registered Imperial PhD students are not eligible
Hold, or be due to receive, a first class or equivalent in an undergraduate or integrated Masters degree
Or hold, or be able to provide evidence of high performance leading to, a distinction in a standalone Master's qualification
Have made contact with a supervisor in an Imperial academic department who has agreed to supervise the research project
Be applying from Imperial College London, the UK or anywhere in the world; there are no nationality restrictions
Be studying full-time or part-time; both are eligible
Candidates with non-traditional academic or career pathways who show strong research potential are encouraged to apply
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to new PhD applicants from Imperial College London, the UK and worldwide with no nationality restrictions, at either full-time or part-time study. Candidates must hold or be predicted a first class or equivalent undergraduate or integrated Master's degree, or a distinction in a standalone Master's qualification, and must have secured a supervisor who has agreed to supervise their research project.
benefits: Full tuition fee funding for 3.5 years
Annual stipend of Â£27,036 (2027-28 rate) for living costs
Consumables fund of Â£2,000 per annum for the first three years
Bespoke opportunities and events from the Early Career Researcher Institute
Full postgraduate support including tailored provision for disabled and international students
Automatic consideration for a standard PhD place if the scholarship is not awarded
coverage: Full funding for tuition fees for 3.5 years
A stipend of Â£27,036 per annum (2027-28 rate) to assist with living costs
A consumables fund of Â£2,000 per annum for the first 3 years of study
A programme of bespoke opportunities and events delivered by the Early Career Researcher Institute (ECRI)
Access to the full range of postgraduate support at Imperial, including tailored support for disabled and international students and ECRI learning and development courses
requirements: Secure agreement to be supervised by an Imperial supervisor before applying, and check the Unavailable Supervisors page
Submit the application through the online admissions system; there is no separate scholarship application form
Select the President's PhD Scholarship option in the funding section of the additional questions tab
Structure the personal statement as two pages: personal statement, then research proposal
Provide two academic referees, excluding the proposed PhD supervisor
Meet any additional application requirements stated by the chosen department
Meet any departmental deadline for academics to put a candidate forward
documents: Application for admission to study at Imperial through the online admissions system
Two-page personal statement: page 1 personal statement, page 2 research proposal
Research proposal document where the department requires more detail
Names of two academic referees who can give an academic reference; the proposed PhD supervisor must not be included
application_method: Imperial College London online postgraduate admissions system, with the scholarship selected in the funding section
Departmental nomination for the scholarship based on academic merit and potential
existing.selection_notes: 50 scholarship places are available and applications are reviewed in two stages: the department reviews candidates meeting or predicted to meet the criteria and shortlists them for the College Selection Panel, which makes the final decision and comprises the Vice-Provost (Research), the Director of the Graduate School and the Faculty Vice-Deans for Research. A Faculty allocation stage scores and ranks departmental shortlists and may make initial offers. Assessment is on academic excellence (past results, transcripts, relative class position, awards, distinctions) and research potential (research experience to date, interest in discovery, research plan and its potential contribution, departmental statement). Applicants not selected for the scholarship are automatically considered for a standard PhD.
existing.best_fit: High-performing new PhD applicants who hold a first class or equivalent degree or a Master's distinction, have secured a supervisor, and can evidence research potential and academic excellence.
existing.notes: The Â£27,036 figure is the 2027-28 annual stipend rate published on the official page; the stipend was Â£26,500 at the 2026-27 rate, so the figure is reviewed annually. The scheme is only open to new PhD applications, and current registered Imperial PhD students cannot be considered. Supervisors are limited to supervising one President's scholar at any time, and a published Unavailable Supervisors page exists. Candidates whose department selects them under the Department Special Case provision should contact the department before applying.
existing.duration: 3.5 years of funding for a PhD place
existing.application_period: 2027-28 entry. Three rounds per academic year with the next deadline on 2 November 2026; funded start dates between 1 August 2027 and 1 November 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Applications for this scholarship scheme are considered at three points in the academic year: apply by 23:59 UK time on 2 November 2026 (award notification by 31 January 2027), by 11 January 2027 (notification by 15 April 2027), or by 1 March 2027 (notification by 31 May 2027). For 2027-28 the earliest start date for a funded place is 1 August 2027 and the latest is 1 November 2027.
existing.program_type: Centrally funded doctoral scholarship scheme for new PhD entrants
